- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast, particularly for mid-to-late horizon.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast at +10–15% above recent peak if sentiment > 0.75.
- Model frequently underestimates in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; add 2–5% buffer to early forecast values.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 75) and sentiment is positive, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change 2–3 days ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% in 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction to next 5-day window.
